classification.difficultyReason: Solve for the intersections, identify the line as the outer radius and integrate the squared-radius difference using the taught method.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The graphs of $xy=5$ and $x+y=6$ are shown. Find their points of intersection.

spec.description: Unshaded first-quadrant hyperbola and descending line, both arrowed at their ends; arrowed coordinate axes without ticks or numerical labels.
spec.mathematics: y=5/x and y=6-x intersect at (1,5) and (5,1). The line lies above the hyperbola between the intersections.
spec.answerVisibility: Curves are supplied; intersection coordinates and curve labels are absent.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}x(6-x)&=5\\x^2-6x+5&=0\\(x-1)(x-5)&=0\\x&=1\text{ or }5.\end{aligned}$$
Using $y=6-x$, the points of intersection are $(1,5)$ and $(5,1)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the volume of the solid generated when the region bounded by the two curves is rotated about the $x$-axis.

answer.worked:
Outer radius $=6-x$; inner radius $=\dfrac{5}{x}$, for $1\le x\le5$.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_1^5\left((6-x)^2-25x^{-2}\right)\,dx\\&=\pi\left[36x-6x^2+\frac{x^3}{3}+\frac{25}{x}\right]_1^5\\&=\pi\left(\frac{230}{3}-\frac{166}{3}\right)\\&=\frac{64\pi}{3}\text{ u}^3.\end{aligned}$$
